newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: RHB Capital growth seen at 20-25 pct.
newsitem.headline: RHB Capital growth seen at 20-25 pct.

text.p: Malaysian financial group RHB Capital Bhd, formerly DCB Holdings Bhd, will see a profit growth of 20-25 percent in 1997 and over the next few years, its executive chairman Rashid Hussain said on Monday.
"We can talk about 20-25 percent (growth). That is what we are very comfortable with," Rashid told Reuters in an interview after the launch of RHB Capital by acting Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim.
He said the group had changed the year-ending to June and in the 1997/98 period, the profit would be substantially higher than 1996/97.

RHB Capital was formally launched on Monday to be the holding company for one of Malaysia's biggest diversified financial services group. This follows the completion on July 1 of Kwong Yik Bank Bhd's merger with DCB.
Sources in RHB said the group's combined profit could exceed one billion ringgit in the current financial year.

For the year to December 31, 1996, RHB Capital, then DCB Holdings, reported a net profit of 349 million ringgit against 279.22 million in the previous year. The pre-tax profit was 564.38 million against 470.92 million.
In the year to June 30, 1996, Kwong Yik Bank Bhd had announced a net profit of 88.98 million ringgit against 67.03 million in the year before.
Kwong Yik will announce its last results shortly, Rashid said.
RHB Capital has total assets of 44.1 billion ringgit ($17.5 billion) and shareholders equity of 3.8 billion ringgit.
RHB Capital is 58 percent owned by Rashid Hussain Bhd following the group's recent restructuring exercise.
